title: Ex-China prices on the rise: Q2 Rare Earths Price Review
gist: Benchmark's Q2 2026 rare earths review shows China PrNd oxide prices falling ~5% off the Q1 peak while heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium) diverged and recovered, driven by a widening ex-China premium as Japan, cut off from direct Chinese heavy rare earth supply since January, bid up prices in the thin European and North American pool.

insights.claim: Benchmark's China PrNd oxide index fell by approximately 5% over Q2 2026, pulling back from the peak levels reached during the robust Q1 rally.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Signals the Q1 rare earth rally lost momentum in Q2 — investors should watch whether PrNd stabilises or continues correcting into Q3.

insights.claim: Heavy rare earths diverged from the broader Q2 downtrend, with dysprosium and terbium staging a meaningful price recovery by the end of the quarter.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Divergence between light (PrNd) and heavy rare earth pricing suggests distinct supply/demand drivers — dysprosium/terbium exposure may outperform PrNd-linked names.
insights.locator: "However, heavy rare earths showed more divergent trends..."

themes.theme: China-Japan heavy rare earth export dynamics

insights.claim: The defining theme of Q2 2026 was a widening gap between Chinese domestic and ex-China heavy rare earth prices, extending a divergence set in motion by China's curbing of rare earth exports to Japan since January 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: An export-restriction-driven price gap is a durable geopolitical trade to track — ex-China heavy rare earth producers and processors stand to benefit from a structurally higher regional price.
insights.locator: "The defining theme of Q2, however, was the widening gulf..."

insights.claim: Japan, the largest consumer of heavy rare earths outside China and historically dependent on direct Chinese supply, spent Q2 2026 aggressively sourcing material from the limited pool available in Europe and North America.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Japanese buyers competing for a small non-Chinese supply pool is a concrete demand signal for Western/allied rare earth processors.
insights.locator: "As the largest consumer of heavy rare earths outside China..."

insights.claim: Japanese buyers' aggressive sourcing progressively bid up ex-China heavy rare earth prices through Q2 2026, while Chinese domestic pricing remained comparatively insulated from the same pressure.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A widening ex-China premium over Chinese domestic pricing is a tradeable structural signal — non-Chinese heavy rare earth supply chains gain relative pricing power.
insights.locator: "...progressively bidding up ex-China prices while Chinese domestic pricing remained comparatively insulated"
